data.summary: This directory is a single scenario definition in an AIO/config generation pipeline that installs the ripgrep search tool. It pairs a declarative metadata file (scenario.toml) that `aio-config gen` consumes for fragment resolution with a Dockerfile fragment that performs the actual idempotent mise-based installation and self-verification of the `rg` binary. Together they form one composable, version-pinned layer of the shell tooling image.

file_insights.name: scenario.toml
file_insights.summary: Declarative scenario metadata describing the ripgrep scenario, its category, installer backend, and pinned versions, consumed by `aio-config gen` for fragment resolution.
file_insights.source_summary: A short TOML document with a leading comment explaining that `aio-config gen` consumes this metadata and that the adjacent fragment.Dockerfile holds the install steps. It defines the keys id, name, description, category, installer, and a single [[versions]] table entry with label and version both set to 15.2.0.
file_insights.detailed_description: This TOML file is the registry entry that the `aio-config gen` tool reads to discover the ripgrep scenario and locate its sibling fragment.Dockerfile. It declares identity (id/name), human-readable description (Chinese, describing ripgrep as a fast recursive grep replacement installed via the mise aqua backend into /opt/mise/installs), classification (category = shell, installer = mise), and a version table used to template the Dockerfile build argument. Without it the fragment would not be resolved or emitted into the generated Dockerfile.
responsibilities: Declare the unique scenario id and display name (ripgrep)
Provide the description and category/installer metadata used by the generator
Pin the concrete tool version (15.2.0) that the fragment templates into the build
Point the generator at the accompanying fragment.Dockerfile for install steps

file_insights.name: fragment.Dockerfile
file_insights.summary: Dockerfile fragment that installs ripgrep at a versioned pin via `mise use -g` and asserts the `rg` binary is resolvable in both login and non-login shells.
file_insights.source_summary: A commented Dockerfile snippet declaring `ARG RIPGREP_VERSION={{version}}` and a single RUN step that runs `mise use -g "ripgrep@${RIPGREP_VERSION}"`, lists the installed tool with `mise ls ripgrep`, and executes bash login/non-login checks that exit 1 with a MISSING message when `rg` is absent. The header comments note that `mise use -g` has read-modify-write semantics, so the fragment is idempotent and composable with other mise tool fragments without aggregation.
file_insights.detailed_description: The fragment is the executable half of the ripgrep scenario: it takes the RIPGREP_VERSION build argument (templated by the generator from scenario.toml) and installs ripgrep globally through mise. It then verifies the installation with `mise ls ripgrep` and two `command -v rg` self-checks (login and non-login shell) to fail the build early if the binary — whose real name is `rg`, not `ripgrep` — is not on PATH. A prominent warning comment documents this binary-name pitfall for future maintainers.
responsibilities: Accept the templated RIPGREP_VERSION build argument from scenario metadata
Install ripgrep globally via the mise aqua backend
Verify the installation is registered with `mise ls ripgrep`
Assert `rg` resolves on PATH in both login and non-login shells, failing the build otherwise
